title: Moonshot AI & Kimi History: From K2 to K3 (2026)
summary: Moonshot AI (月之暗面) was founded in Beijing in March 2023 by Yang Zhilin, Zhou Xinyu and Wu Yuxin. Every Kimi model to K3, each funding round, and the K3 design.
body_markdown:
Moonshot AI is a Beijing artificial intelligence company that builds the Kimi family of models with one stubborn belief: **open models can be as good as the closed frontier — and everyone should be able to download them.** In three years it went from a long-context chatbot nobody outside China had heard of to **Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model** that trades blows with the best proprietary systems on Earth, released through the API on July 16, 2026, with full open weights on July 27.


How does a startup named after a Pink Floyd album end up shipping one of the most capable open models in the world? Who is Yang Zhilin, and why did Alibaba lead a billion-dollar round in his company before it was a year old? And what actually changed between Kimi K2, K2.5, and K3? Let's wind back the clock. 🌘


> **TL;DR:** Moonshot AI was founded in **March 2023** in Beijing by Yang Zhilin, Zhou Xinyu, and Wu Yuxin. Its Kimi chatbot broke out on long context; **Kimi K2** (July 2025) became the "open-weight DeepSeek moment"; **Kimi K3** (July 16, 2026) is a **2.8-trillion-parameter** open-weight flagship at frontier level. A July 2026 round reportedly valued the company at about **$35 billion** .[Clone a live AI-lab tracker →](https://www.taskade.com/app/finance-tracker-dashboard-tmnju1vsp3ggajo7) and follow every model launch yourself.


**Moonshot AI history in one paragraph:** Moonshot AI started in Beijing in March 2023, on the 50th anniversary of *The Dark Side of the Moon* . It launched the Kimi chatbot in October 2023 with a 200,000-character context window, raised a $1 billion Alibaba-led round in February 2024, open-sourced the 1-trillion-parameter Kimi K2 in July 2025, and shipped the 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 in July 2026.


**What is Moonshot AI's Chinese name?** Moonshot AI's Chinese name is **月之暗面** (Yuè Zhī Ànmiàn), "the dark side of the moon," after Pink Floyd's 1973 album *The Dark Side of the Moon* , a nod to founder **杨植麟 (Yang Zhilin)** . The registered company is **北京月之暗面科技有限公司** (Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co., Ltd.), founded in Beijing in March 2023.


The[TSK-1 Benchmark](https://www.taskade.com/tsk) sends the same app request to each model and records whether the app worked, and the[Kimi results](https://www.taskade.com/tsk/kimi) show how Kimi did.


For the other labs that shaped open-weight AI in China, read the[DeepSeek history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/deepseek-ai-history) and the[Qwen history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/alibaba-qwen-history) .


## What Is Moonshot AI?


Moonshot AI is a Chinese AI company founded in **March 2023** in Beijing, best known for the **Kimi** family of large language models. It is counted among China's "six AI Tigers" — the cohort of well-funded startups racing to build frontier models — and it is the one that bet hardest on **open weights** : models whose parameters you can download, run locally, and fine-tune, rather than only rent through an API.


That bet is the whole story. Where much of the industry raced to lock capability behind paid endpoints, Moonshot's founder framed the mission differently at NVIDIA's GTC 2026 keynote:


> "One of our major pursuits is to build better open models and we believe in democratizing intelligence. Open models cannot be just open. They have to also be great."
>
>
> — Yang Zhilin, GTC 2026 keynote

### Who Owns Moonshot AI?


Moonshot AI is a private company controlled by its founders, with co-founder and CEO **Yang Zhilin** at the top and **Alibaba** as the largest outside investor. Alibaba's annual report disclosed about **US$0.8 billion for an approximately 36% stake** taken in its 2024 fiscal year. Every round since has diluted that share, so the current figure is lower and undisclosed.


The structure has three layers, according to company records reviewed by[The Wire China](https://www.thewirechina.com/2025/09/28/who-is-moonshot-ai/) : the founders hold the Beijing operating company directly, other operations sit under a Hong Kong holding company, and that holding company's only shareholder is the Cayman Islands-registered Moonshot AI Ltd. Outside capital arrives at the offshore level. Some profiles also list **Zhang Yutao** as a co-founder alongside the three names on the founding record.

## What Is Kimi?


Kimi is both **a chatbot** (the consumer app at kimi.com) and **a family of models** (Kimi v1 through Kimi K3). The two share a name because they share an origin: **Kimi is founder Yang Zhilin's English nickname.** The chatbot launched on October 9, 2023, opened to the public on November 16, 2023, and made its name on one feature nobody else did as well at the time — reading enormous documents without losing the thread.


Think of it this way: the chatbot is the product a person opens in a browser; the model is the engine underneath, which Moonshot also publishes so developers can run it themselves. When people say "Kimi beat the previous best open model," they mean the model. When they say "I asked Kimi to summarize a 200-page contract," they mean the chatbot.


## Why the Names "Moonshot" and "Kimi"?


Moonshot AI's Chinese name is **月之暗面** (Yuè Zhī Ànmiàn), which literally means **"Dark Side of the Moon"** — a direct nod to the 1973 Pink Floyd album. The English name "Moonshot" carries the Silicon Valley meaning: an audacious, long-odds project aimed at a giant payoff. Put the two together and you get the company's self-image — an ambitious shot at something most people think is out of reach.


The timing was deliberate too. *The Dark Side of the Moon* came out in March 1973, it is Yang's favorite album, and Moonshot AI launched in March 2023, on the album's 50th anniversary. The legal entity followed on April 17, 2023, which is why a few registries list April as the founding month.


The model name is more personal. **Kimi is Yang Zhilin's own English nickname** , and it stuck to the chatbot and then to the whole model line. It's a rare case where the founder's name literally became the product — and a small reminder that behind the benchmark tables sits a specific person with a specific research history.


## Who Founded Moonshot AI? Meet Yang Zhilin


Moonshot AI was founded in **March 2023** by **Yang Zhilin** (杨植麟, CEO), **Zhou Xinyu** , and **Wu Yuxin** . Yang is the technical center of gravity, and his research pedigree is the reason serious investors took the company seriously from day one.


Yang earned his PhD at **Carnegie Mellon University** , advised by Ruslan Salakhutdinov and William Cohen, and did stints connected to Google Brain and Meta AI. Crucially, he co-authored two papers that anyone who studies language models will recognize:


- **Transformer-XL** — an architecture that extended how far a model could "remember" across long inputs, foreshadowing Moonshot's later obsession with long context.
- **XLNet** (NeurIPS 2019) — a pretraining method that **outperformed Google's BERT on 20 tasks** and became one of the most-cited NLP papers of its era.


Moonshot AI's Chinese name, 月之暗面, means "Dark Side of the Moon" — a Pink Floyd reference. Founder Yang Zhilin's English nickname, Kimi, became the model line's name. Photo: NASA / public domain.


The takeaway for the history: **Moonshot didn't stumble into long context and efficient architectures.** Those were Yang's research themes years before the company existed. When Kimi's first breakout feature turned out to be reading enormous documents, it was a founder building the thing he'd studied his whole career.

### Zhou Xinyu and Wu Yuxin: The Other Two Founders


Moonshot AI's two other founders bring the engineering half of the story, and both came from computer vision rather than language. Here is what each one did before 2023.

His record is about making large networks cheap enough to run, a theme that returns in K3's 4-bit weights.

With Kaiming He he co-authored **Group Normalization** , he co-authored **MoCo** (Momentum Contrast), and he created **Detectron2** , one of the most used open-source vision libraries. ## Moonshot AI History, Era by Era (2023–2026)


Moonshot AI's history falls into five eras: a founding sprint in 2023, a consumer long-context boom in 2024, an open-weight pivot after the DeepSeek shock in 2025, the agent-swarm and funding surge of early 2026, and the Kimi K3 frontier era from July 2026. Each era changed what the company sold and who paid for it.


### Era 1: The Founding Sprint (March to December 2023)


Moonshot AI went from zero to a shipped product in seven months. Yang, Zhou and Wu started the company in March 2023, registered it on April 17, and closed a seed round from HongShan (the former Sequoia China) and ZhenFund that valued it near $300 million, according to PitchBook data cited by the *South China Morning Post* . Reported seed totals range from about $60 million to $200 million.


On **October 9, 2023** , Kimi Chat launched with a context window of **200,000 Chinese characters** , about 128,000 tokens, at a time when most Chinese chatbots handled a few thousand. It opened to everyone on **November 16, 2023** . The pitch was concrete: paste a contract, a thesis or a codebase, and ask questions about all of it.

### Era 2: The Long-Context Boom (2024)


2024 was the year Kimi became a household name in China and Moonshot became one of the "AI Tigers." In **February 2024** Moonshot raised more than **$1 billion** in a round led by **Alibaba** and HongShan at about a **$2.5 billion** valuation, the largest single round for a Chinese LLM startup on public record at the time, per[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2024/02/21/moonshot-ai-funding-china/) . Alibaba put in about $800 million of it.


In **March 2024** Moonshot announced a **2-million-character** context window, ten times the launch figure. The demand spike that followed briefly overwhelmed Kimi's servers. In **August 2024** , **Tencent** and **Gaorong Capital** joined a round of more than $300 million at about **$3.3 billion** , according to[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-08-05/tencent-joins-300-million-financing-for-china-s-ai-unicorn) . Kimi Explore, an autonomous search mode, followed in October.


Behind the chatbot, Moonshot published **Mooncake** in June 2024, the serving system that splits prompt processing (prefill) from token generation (decode) and pools a shared cache across CPU, DRAM and SSD. Mooncake later won the Erik Riedel Best Paper Award at USENIX FAST 2025. It is the same disaggregation idea that hosts use to serve K3 today, covered in theK3 serving section below.

### Era 3: The DeepSeek Shock and the Open-Weight Pivot (2025)


The year began badly. On **January 20, 2025** , Moonshot released **Kimi K1.5** , a reasoning model it said matched OpenAI's o1 on math and code. DeepSeek released R1 within hours of it. R1 shipped open weights, and K1.5 did not, so R1 took the world's attention. Analyst Tony Peng told The Wire China that Moonshot "lost steam" after the DeepSeek splash, and Kimi's rank among Chinese AI apps by monthly active users slipped through the first half of the year.


Moonshot answered by opening up. In February it published "Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" (arXiv 2502.16982) with an open 16B-parameter model. Open-weight vision, audio and coding models followed between April and June, and the Kimi-Researcher agent arrived in June. Then, on **July 11, 2025** , came **Kimi K2** : 1 trillion parameters, 32 billion active, trained on **15.5 trillion tokens** with zero loss spikes, and released under a modified MIT license. It ranked as the top open model on the LMSYS Arena leaderboard within a week, according to the[K2 technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20534) .


The rest of 2025 was a release cadence most labs could not match: **K2-Instruct-0905** in September with a 256K context, the **OK Computer** agent mode the same month, **Kimi Linear** on October 30, and **K2 Thinking** on November 6. CNBC reported, citing one source, that K2 Thinking cost about **$4.6 million** to train. Moonshot researchers later said that was not an official figure. On December 31, Yang told staff in an internal letter that Moonshot had closed a **$500 million** round led by **IDG Capital** at a **$4.3 billion** valuation.


### Era 4: Agent Swarms and the Funding Surge (January to June 2026)


**Kimi K2.5** , released on **January 27, 2026** , added native vision and the **agent swarm** and became a favorite base for coding products. In March, after a developer found the model ID in Cursor's API, a Moonshot researcher questioned the credit. Cursor then confirmed that its **Composer 2** coding model was built on K2.5, and Cursor co-founder Aman Sanger called the missing credit "a miss." Moonshot's account later said the use was part of an authorized commercial partnership through Fireworks AI.


The money moved faster than the models. Reports put a round of more than **$700 million** at a **$10 billion** valuation in February. At NVIDIA GTC in March, Yang presented the three scaling dimensions behind K2.5 and previewed **Attention Residuals** (arXiv 2603.15031, March 16, 2026). **K2.6** shipped on **April 20** , and on **May 7** Moonshot closed about **$2 billion** at more than **$20 billion** , led by Meituan's Long-Z Investments, per[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/07/chinas-moonshot-ai-raises-2b-at-20b-valuation-as-demand-for-open-source-ai-skyrockets/) . TechCrunch reported annual recurring revenue above $200 million in April. **K2.7 Code** followed on **June 12** .


### Era 5: Kimi K3 and the Frontier (July 2026 to Today)


On **July 16, 2026** , Moonshot launched **Kimi K3** through its API and app, and on **July 27** it released the weights and the technical report. Artificial Analysis then called K3 "the leading open weights model" with a score of **57** on its Intelligence Index. Two days later, on **July 29** , Bloomberg reported that Moonshot had closed about **$3.5 billion** at a **$35 billion** valuation, nearly twice its target, with China's National Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund among the leads, per[TechNode](https://technode.com/2026/07/30/moonshot-ai-reportedly-closes-3-5-billion-round-at-35-billion-valuation/) .[TechNode](https://technode.com/2026/07/22/moonshot-ai-reportedly-plans-final-pre-ipo-round-at-50-billion-valuation/) , citing Bloomberg, reported that annual recurring revenue rose from $100 million in March to $300 million in June.


The same weeks brought the sharpest scrutiny the company has faced: a White House accusation of distillation, then an Anthropic threat report in September. Both are covered inControversies and Open Questions below.

### Kimi v1 (2023): The Long-Context Breakout


The original **Kimi chatbot** launched in late 2023, and its calling card was **long context** — the ability to read and reason over very large documents in a single go. In a market where most assistants choked on anything past a few thousand words, "paste a whole book and ask questions" was a genuine differentiator, and it earned Moonshot an early, loyal Chinese user base. If you want the deeper mechanics of why context length matters so much, see[how large language models actually work](https://www.taskade.com/blog/how-do-llms-work) .


### Kimi K1.5 (January 2025): Reasoning Arrives


**K1.5** brought explicit **reasoning** — the model "thinks" through a problem in intermediate steps before answering, the same shift that reshaped the whole field around[reasoning models](https://www.taskade.com/blog/reasoning-models) . It was Moonshot signaling that it intended to keep pace with the reasoning wave, not just win on document length.


### Kimi K2 (July 2025): The Open-Weight "DeepSeek Moment"


**Kimi K2** , released **July 11, 2025** , is where Moonshot became a global name. It was a **1-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model** with roughly **32 billion active parameters** , and it shipped with **open weights** under a modified-MIT license. The reaction echoed the earlier shock of DeepSeek: here was near-frontier agentic and coding capability that anyone could *download* , not merely rent. Commentators called it an "open-weight DeepSeek moment," and it reframed Moonshot from "the long-context lab" into "the lab pushing the open frontier."


Under the hood, K2 was a deliberately conservative design. Its[technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20534) describes an architecture similar to DeepSeek-V3: **61 layers** , Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), **384 experts with 8 routed per token plus 1 shared expert** , and a 160K-token vocabulary. The new part was the optimizer. Moonshot trained K2 on **15.5 trillion tokens** with **MuonClip** , its version of the Muon optimizer, and reported zero loss spikes across the whole run. K2 reported 65.8% on SWE-bench Verified in single-attempt agentic mode, a strong open-model result in July 2025.


### Kimi K2 Instruct & K2 Thinking (September–November 2025)


Through late 2025 Moonshot iterated fast, shipping **instruction-tuned** and **reasoning** variants of K2 and extending context toward 256K tokens. This is the period where the K2 family hardened into a serious tool for agentic workflows rather than a research demo.


**K2-Instruct-0905** (September 2025) doubled the context window from 128K to 256K tokens and improved agentic coding. **K2 Thinking** (November 6, 2025) was the bigger step. Moonshot trained it with quantization-aware training so it runs natively in **INT4** , which roughly doubled generation speed, and it kept a coherent plan across **200 to 300 consecutive tool calls** , where earlier models drifted after 30 to 50. On its own model card Moonshot reported **44.9% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools** , **60.2% on BrowseComp** and **71.3% on SWE-bench Verified** .


### Kimi K2.5 (January 2026): Multimodal + the Agent Swarm


**K2.5** is the pivot most competitors under-cover, and it's the technical heart of everything that followed. Two things changed at once.


First, **native vision through "early fusion."** Instead of training a text model and bolting on an image module later ("late fusion"), K2.5 trained on vision and text tokens together from the start, giving one shared understanding. Moonshot described it as **the first open model with native joint vision-and-text capabilities** , and reported a striking result: with a strong text base, it needed essentially **zero vision fine-tuning data** to reach near-state-of-the-art on vision tasks.


Second, the **agent swarm.** Rather than one agent grinding through a task step by step, a lead orchestrator spawns **many parallel sub-agents** — researchers, coders, fact-checkers — that work simultaneously and report back. Yang's analogy in the GTC keynote was a company: "if we build a company, we need maybe a CEO to decompose and assign the task to different roles." We'll visualize it in a moment.


K2.5 kept the K2 skeleton (1 trillion parameters, 32 billion active, 384 experts) and added a 400-million-parameter vision encoder called **MoonViT** . Moonshot continued pre-training from a K2 checkpoint on about 15 trillion more mixed vision and text tokens, on NVIDIA H800 GPUs, as Yang described at GTC. At launch Moonshot said the swarm could run up to **100 sub-agents** and **1,500 tool calls** in parallel, cutting wall-clock time by up to 4.5 times on wide search tasks. The model shipped with a command-line coding agent, **Kimi Code** , and four app modes: Instant, Thinking, Agent and Agent Swarm (beta).


### Kimi K2.6 & K2.7 Code (April–June 2026): The Agentic-Coding Push


The **K2.6** and **K2.7 Code** releases specialized hard on **agentic coding** — long, multi-step programming tasks run with minimal supervision. On Moonshot's reported evaluations, the K2 family climbed to the top of open-weight agentic-coding leaderboards, and K2.6 became one of the models teams reached for when they wanted a cheap, capable open coder. (Kimi's K2.6 is one of the Moonshot models available in Taskade's model stack today.)


**K2.6** (April 20, 2026) raised the swarm ceiling to **300 sub-agents and 4,000 coordinated steps** and was released under the same modified MIT license. **K2.7 Code** (June 12, 2026) was a coding specialist built on K2.6. Moonshot reported a 21.8% gain on its own Kimi Code Bench v2 and about 30% fewer reasoning tokens than K2.6, and made it the default model in Kimi Code. Both kept the 1-trillion-parameter, 256K-context design that K3 would replace a month later.


### Kimi K3 (July 2026): The 2.8T Open-Weight Flagship


**Kimi K3** , released **July 16, 2026** , is the payoff. It is a **2.8-trillion-parameter** mixture-of-experts model that activates **16 routed + 2 shared of its 896 experts per token** — about **104B of its 2.8T parameters, roughly 3.7%** — so a model that huge runs at a fraction of the compute a dense 2.8T model would need. It has **native vision** and a **1-million-token context window** , and Moonshot reports roughly **2.5× better scaling efficiency than K2** .


The API went live immediately, and the **full open weights were released on July 27, 2026** , together with the tech report. Moonshot publishes per-token pricing for the K3 API on its[API platform](https://platform.kimi.ai/) .


Independent reviewers who stress-tested K3 at launch reached a consistent verdict: it is at or near frontier level for agentic coding and long-horizon autonomy, trading blows with the strongest proprietary models on many tasks — while still showing rough edges (it can be slow and token-hungry). One reviewer's summary captured the moment: *"Open-source AI is no longer a few months behind the closed frontier models."* Moonshot's own release note is honest about the gap that remains — the model "still trails the most powerful proprietary models" on the very hardest tasks — but the direction is unmistakable. ## How Kimi's Agent Swarm Works


The agent swarm is Moonshot's answer to a simple problem: some tasks are too big for one agent to finish in a reasonable time. Instead of a single model working sequentially, a **lead orchestrator decomposes the goal and spawns parallel sub-agents** — Yang described scaling to **100 or even 1,000** of them — each handling a slice of the work, then reports get merged into one result.


To train this behavior, Moonshot shaped three rewards so the swarm doesn't cheat or collapse: an **instantiation reward** (pay the model for spawning sub-agents so it doesn't quietly revert to a single agent), a **finish reward** (pay it only when sub-tasks actually complete, so it can't spawn junk it never finishes), and an **outcome reward** (did the overall task succeed). If the "orchestrator plus specialists" pattern sounds familiar, it's the same idea behind[multi-agent platforms](https://www.taskade.com/blog/best-multi-agent-platforms) and[inter-agent communication patterns](https://www.taskade.com/blog/inter-agent-communication-patterns) — Moonshot just baked it into the model's training.


## Kimi's Architecture in Plain English


You don't need a PhD to understand what makes Kimi efficient. Moonshot's whole pitch, laid out in Yang's GTC 2026 keynote, is that **scaling is the main driver of progress** — and that you can scale along more than just "train on more data." Kimi pushes three dimensions:


- **Token efficiency (MuonClip).** The optimizer decides how to nudge a model's weights each training step. Moonshot invested heavily in the **Muon** optimizer and its own **MuonClip** variant, which stabilizes training at trillion-parameter scale (past a certain size, internal scores "explode" and training diverges; a clipping trick caps them without hurting accuracy). Moonshot reports **roughly 2× the token efficiency of the long-standing Adam optimizer** — meaning the same limited pile of high-quality data teaches the model about twice as much. As Yang put it: *"Token efficiency is not just about efficiency. It's actually also about improving the upper bound of intelligence."*
- **Long context (Kimi Linear + Kimi Delta Attention).** A more efficient way to relate words across a very long input, so the model can hold a **1-million-token** window (about 700,000 words) without the cost exploding. This is the through-line from the original 2023 chatbot to K3.
- **Attention residuals.** A next-generation architectural idea Moonshot previewed at GTC, reported to add **~24% more token efficiency** . Combined with MuonClip, it's much of where K3's ~2.5× scaling gain comes from.


The important context-setting caveat: these efficiency figures (2×, 24%) are **Moonshot's own reported results** from its papers and keynote, not independent consensus — and the underlying Muon optimizer originated outside Moonshot (with researcher Keller Jordan in late 2024). Moonshot's contribution is scaling it. For a broader tour of these building blocks, our[open-source LLM history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/open-source-llm-history) walks the full lineage.


Yang's own 40-minute walkthrough is the best primary source on these three ideas. He explains the QK-Clip fix that stopped K2's attention scores from exploding past 1,000, the per-channel forgetting in Kimi Delta Attention, the three swarm rewards, and the first public look at Attention Residuals.

### Kimi Delta Attention: How K3 Holds a Million Tokens


Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) is a linear attention that stores a fixed-size memory per conversation instead of a cache that grows with every token. Standard softmax attention keeps a key and a value for every past token, so a 1-million-token conversation means a huge cache that the GPU must read for each new token. KDA keeps one small matrix per attention head and edits it as tokens arrive.


KDA is the latest step in a line of research that started outside Moonshot. Each step fixed the weakness of the one before it:


Step Year What it stores What it fixed


**Softmax attention** 2017 A key and value for every past token The original Transformer design


**Linear attention** (Katharopoulos et al.) 2020 One fixed d × d state per head Constant memory, but recall fades as the state fills


**DeltaNet / delta rule** 2021–2024 Same state, edited instead of summed Overwrites the value stored under a key


**Parallel delta rule** (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2024) 2024 Same Rewrites the recurrence as big matrix multiplies that GPUs run fast


**Gated DeltaNet** (ICLR 2025) 2025 Same, plus one forget gate Forgets old context when the topic changes


**Kimi Delta Attention** (Moonshot) 2025 Same, with a forget rate per channel Some channels hold long memory while others refresh fast


A pure linear model forgets details that a full-attention model keeps, which is why K3 is a **hybrid** . One layer in four is a Gated MLA full-attention layer that can still look back at any exact token. Moonshot's[Kimi Linear paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26692) reported that a 3-to-1 mix of KDA and MLA beat full attention on short-context, long-input and long-output tasks while decoding long contexts much faster. For the basics of attention and caching, see the wiki entries on the[attention mechanism](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/attention-mechanism) , the[KV cache](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/kv-cache) and the[context window](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/context-window) , plus our[history of the context window](https://www.taskade.com/blog/context-window-history) .


### Attention Residuals: Attention Turned 90 Degrees


Attention Residuals replace the residual connection, the plain "add the previous layer's output" step that every Transformer has used since ResNet. In a normal model, layer 50 receives the equal-weight sum of everything before it and cannot choose. With Attention Residuals each layer has a learned query that scores earlier block outputs and mixes them by score, for example 90% from one block and 10% from another.


Yang described it at GTC as attention "rotated by 90 degrees": attention across depth instead of across tokens. To keep the memory cost down, Moonshot groups layers into blocks and attends only over block outputs, which it calls Block AttnRes. The[Attention Residuals paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15031) (March 16, 2026) reported the gain held across model sizes, and Yang put it at about **24% better token efficiency** .


### Stable LatentMoE: 896 Experts Without Collapse


A mixture-of-experts layer sends each token to a few specialist sub-networks, called experts, instead of the whole model. The risk is a rich-get-richer loop: an expert that wins a few early tokens trains faster, wins more tokens, and ends up doing most of the work while others sit idle. K3's **Stable LatentMoE** balances load across 896 experts and normalizes the very wide hidden activations that would otherwise overflow low-precision math. The[mixture of experts](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/mixture-of-experts) wiki entry covers the basics.


The jump in sparsity is large. K2 picked 8 of 384 experts (about 1 in 48), and K3 picks 16 of 896 (about 1 in 56), plus 2 shared experts every token uses. That is how a 2.8-trillion-parameter model computes only about 104 billion parameters per token.

## How to Serve Kimi K3: Total Parameters Set the Bill


Serving Kimi K3 is a memory problem first. The native checkpoint is about **1.56 TB** in MXFP4, and every expert must stay in GPU memory, because at production batch sizes every expert is in use at some instant and swapping experts in and out breaks latency targets. Total parameters, not the ~104 billion active ones, decide how many GPUs you need.


```text
KIMI K3 CHECKPOINT: ~1.56 TB (MXFP4 weights)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
8 x H100  (80 GB each)   =   640 GB   NO   (less than half)
8 x B200  (180 GB each)  = 1,440 GB   NO   (about 120 GB short)
8 x B300  (288 GB each)  = 2,304 GB   YES  (~740 GB left for cache)
Per B300 at TP8:  ~183 GB experts + 9 GB attention
+ 6 GB other weights + ~90 GB free
= 288 GB


```


The per-GPU budget above is the one Baseten's engineers drew on a whiteboard in their walkthrough of K3 serving. Their talk is the clearest public explanation of how a trillion-parameter model actually runs, from the linear-attention math to the two caches.


### Two Ways to Split K3 Across Eight GPUs


Hosts choose between two layouts. **Tensor parallelism (TP8)** slices every layer evenly across eight GPUs: best single-user latency, but the most cross-GPU traffic. **Tensor plus expert parallelism (TP + EP)** keeps attention sliced but places whole experts on specific GPUs, which raises total throughput. Hosts then add **expert load balancing** , extra copies of the busiest experts, because real traffic never matches the training mix. Baseten's[day-zero K3 post](https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-to-build-a-day-zero-api-for-kimi-k3/) (July 27, 2026) describes running K3 on GB300 NVL72 systems with 8 GPUs per replica.


### The Hybrid Cache: Two Allocators, Not One


K3's hybrid attention forces a new kind of cache. The 24 MLA layers keep a per-token cache, and the 69 KDA layers keep a fixed-size state per conversation, so the inference engine runs two allocators with different eviction rules.


Cache pool Layers Size Grows with tokens?


**MLA KV cache** 24 Gated MLA layers 576 values per layer, about 13.5 KiB per token in FP8 Yes, linearly


**KDA recurrent state** 69 KDA layers About 217 MB per conversation in BF16, about 27 MB per GPU at TP8 No, fixed size


The catch is prefix caching. When two requests share a long prompt, the MLA cache can be reused up to the exact token, but a KDA state is valid only at the exact token where it was saved. The engine must resume from the nearest saved checkpoint, so prefix caching on a hybrid model is coarser than on a pure-attention model.


Hosts also split **prefill** (reading the prompt) and **decode** (writing the answer) onto separate GPU pools, the same disaggregation Moonshot's Mooncake paper described in 2024. For agentic and long-context traffic they add more prefill capacity. Decode speed is limited by[memory bandwidth](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/infrastructure/memory-bandwidth) , because every new token reads the cache from[HBM](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/infrastructure/hbm) : a B300 moves about 8 TB/s per GPU, against 3.35 TB/s for an H100. Speculative decoding with draft models such as EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark then raises per-user[tokens per second](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/tokens-per-second) , but a draft model trains on the target model's hidden states, so it only arrives after the main model runs in production.

## Is Kimi Open Source? The Modified-MIT License, Explained


Here's the nuance almost every write-up gets muddy. The **Kimi K2 family shipped with open weights under a modified-MIT license** — you can download the parameters, run them locally, and fine-tune them. The single condition is an **attribution clause** : commercial products that cross **100 million monthly active users or $20 million in monthly revenue** must display "Kimi" prominently in their interface.


Two precisions worth keeping straight:


1. **Open weight ≠ fully open source.** Moonshot releases the *weights* , not the full training data or pipeline. "Open weight" is the accurate term; it's more open than an API-only model and less open than a fully reproducible release.
2. **License varies by version.** The headline modified-MIT terms apply to the K2 open-weight line. **Kimi K3 ships under Moonshot's own Kimi K3 License** , a separate document, not modified MIT. So **check the specific license attached to each model version** before you build on it. When in doubt, read the model card.

### The Distillation Dispute (2026)


The most serious open question is whether Moonshot used outputs from American models to train Kimi without permission. Training one model on another model's answers is called[model distillation](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/model-distillation) , and it is legitimate when the owner allows it. ## 💬 Frequently Asked Questions About Moonshot AI & Kimi


What is Moonshot AI?


Moonshot AI is a Chinese AI company founded in March 2023 in Beijing, best known for the Kimi family of large language models. It's one of China's "six AI Tigers" and the lab that bet hardest on open weights, culminating in the 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 in July 2026.


Who founded Moonshot AI?


Yang Zhilin (CEO), Zhou Xinyu, and Wu Yuxin founded the company in March 2023. Yang holds a PhD from Carnegie Mellon and co-authored the influential Transformer-XL and XLNet papers, the latter of which beat Google's BERT on 20 tasks in 2019.


Why is it called Moonshot and Kimi?


The Chinese name 月之暗面 means "Dark Side of the Moon," a Pink Floyd reference; "Moonshot" is the English rendering of an audacious goal. "Kimi" is founder Yang Zhilin's English nickname, which became the name of the chatbot and model family.


What was Kimi K2 and why did it matter?


Kimi K2 (July 11, 2025) was a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight mixture-of-experts model that delivered near-frontier agentic and coding performance you could download and run. It was widely called an "open-weight DeepSeek moment" and made Moonshot a global name.


What is Kimi K3?


Kimi K3 (July 16, 2026) is Moonshot's flagship: a 2.8-trillion-parameter MoE model activating 16 routed + 2 shared of 896 experts per token (about 104B active, roughly 3.7%), with native vision and a 1-million-token context window. The API launched immediately, and the full open weights were released on July 27, 2026, under the Kimi K3 License.


Is Kimi open source or open weight?


Open weight. The K2 family shipped under a modified-MIT license — you can download and fine-tune the model — with an attribution clause for very large commercial products. The training data and full pipeline aren't released, so "open weight" is more accurate than "fully open source." The license varies by version: Kimi K3 ships under Moonshot's own Kimi K3 License.


How much is Moonshot AI worth?


A roughly $3.5 billion round that closed in late July 2026 reportedly valued the company at about $35 billion, after about $20 billion in May 2026 and $4.3 billion at the end of 2025. Reported rounds since 2023 add up to more than $8 billion. Alibaba is the largest outside backer, with an approximately 36% stake taken in 2024 and diluted since. AI valuations move fast, so treat that figure as a dated snapshot.


Who owns Moonshot AI?


Moonshot AI is private and controlled by its founders, led by CEO Yang Zhilin. Alibaba is the largest outside investor, and Tencent, HongShan, IDG Capital, 5Y Capital, Gaorong Capital, Meituan's Long-Z Investments, China Mobile and China's National AI Industry Investment Fund also hold stakes.


Is Kimi a Chinese AI?


Yes. Kimi is built by Moonshot AI, headquartered in Haidian District, Beijing. Its operating company is Beijing Moonshot AI Technology Co., Ltd. (北京月之暗面科技有限公司). The open-weight Kimi models can be downloaded and hosted anywhere, including by US cloud providers.


Who are Zhou Xinyu and Wu Yuxin?


They are Moonshot AI's other two founders, both Tsinghua graduates. Zhou Xinyu co-authored ShuffleNet during years at the vision company Megvii. Wu Yuxin co-authored Group Normalization with Kaiming He and created the Detectron2 library at Meta's AI research lab.


When was Kimi K3 released, and what is its architecture?


Kimi K3 launched through the API on July 16, 2026, and its open weights and technical report followed on July 27. It is a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with about 104 billion active parameters, 93 layers (69 Kimi Delta Attention plus 24 Gated MLA), Attention Residuals, 16 of 896 experts per token plus 2 shared, a 1-million-token context, and native MXFP4 weights.


What hardware does Kimi K3 need?


The checkpoint is about 1.56 TB, so it fits one 8-GPU NVIDIA B300 node but not an 8-GPU B200 or H100 node. Every expert must stay loaded, so total parameters, not active ones, set the hardware bill. Most teams use K3 through a hosted API instead.


Was Kimi K3 distilled from Claude?


That is disputed. Anthropic and the White House have accused Moonshot of distilling US models, and Moonshot staff rejected the claim about K3 and Claude Fable. No public evidence settles it as of October 2026.

It depends on the task.
